questions.question: Which ship, exactly, was pirated from Scarem Montem?
questions.context: While planning Wilhelm's 1224 return trip, the table half-remembered that one of the covenant's own ships was originally taken from Scarem Montem — but didn't pin down which one, or the circumstances. Two candidates surface elsewhere in the chronicle but neither is confirmed: the Maelstrom's Maw (its original acquisition by Nequam is never described) and the Hound of Cassel (a raided prize ship from an unnamed rival covenant, not stated to be Scarem Montem's).

questions.question: What's the current status of the Maelstrom's Maw?
questions.context: Originally Nequam of Tytalus's ship, handed off to Kor Ex Flambeau in Summer 1220. Per "Debates about Valerian, new Tribunal, Chests, etc" (Winter 1221-22): "Kor's Absence: His ship did not come in, and the Master's Chart no longer tracks it." Neither Nequam nor Kor appear in the covenant's current active-magi roster — this reads as the last confirmed sighting of both the magus and the ship, with nothing since reactivating either. Lost, or just gone quiet?
questions.raised_event: The handoff of the Maelstrom's Maw

questions.question: Is the "Adamant" the same ship as the fleet's fifth hull, commissioned at Bergen and given to Valerian?
questions.context: "Sorting through Solving's letters..." (Spring 1220) has a shipwright's letter announcing the fifth and final ship of the fleet is complete at Bergen. "Valerian's Arrival" (Spring 1222) has Valerian "given the newly purchased fifth ship and skeleton crew." The name "Adamant" only appears later, in the Fall 1223 travel-planning material — the identification is a strong inference from the timeline, not something stated outright anywhere in-text.

questions.question: What happened to the Hound of Cassel — the ship captured in the Summer 1221 piracy raid?
questions.context: Raided from an unnamed rival sea-trading covenant by Valdemar's crew; yielded three magically-sealed chests and the letter that led to discovering the imprisoned Valerian de Castellane. Text has the party debating "keep as prize or sink," leaning toward "find a shadow port for sale" — but no later event confirms whether it was sold, kept, or renamed. Possibly relevant to q001 (the ship pirated from Scarem Montem) if it was never actually sold off.

questions.question: Is "The Scholar's Wake" still an active covenant ship, and which hull does Stijntje/Dustin actually sail on to Ireland?
questions.context: The Scholar's Wake (Stijntje's original recruiting ship, Spring 1220; also where Valerian's belongings teleported in on his arrival, Spring 1222) doesn't appear again in the text after that — unclear if it's still active in 1223 or has been folded into general "the fleet" references. Relatedly: the Fall 1223 travel plan names only the Brineborn (Éogan, Wilhelm, Hilda, one assistant) and the Adamant (Valerian, Dietrich, two assistants); a later addendum has Dustin opting in and bringing Stijntje, without re-stating which hull they board. Brineborn is the reasonable assumption but isn't textually explicit.
questions.raised_event: Ireland travel plan finalized: Dublin, the coast, and wintering near Carrick
